description: S451 ("your recs on all five" item 1, R1 wins): the `<request>` twin of server-fn/error-boundary-fallback. Server data reaches markup through a `<request>`, not a render-time call inside an `<errorBoundary>` (which is E-VALUE-SERVER-CALL, §13.7 — see server-fn/error-boundary-value-server-call-neg). loadName(id)! LoadError touches a server resource (escalates); the server answers with the impl-neutral error directive {"__serverError": {type:"LoadError", variant:"Timeout"}}. The request settles to failure: `<#nameLoad>.error` is set, so .eb-fallback renders; `<#nameLoad>.data` stays absent, so .eb-name is not in the DOM; @name keeps its initial value; siblings render (.eb-header, .eb-footer). No E-ERROR-* fires: the `<request>` body's call is handled by the request (§19.4.3 item 5), and no E-VALUE-SERVER-CALL fires (a `<request>` body is an action position, §6.15 / §13.7).
rationale: §19.6.1 Scope / §13.7 (S451): server data enters markup through `<request>`; its failure surfaces on `<#id>.error`. §6.7.7 settled(failure): .error -> the caught error value, .data retains its prior value (not, on first mount), the success cell is left untouched. §19.9.1: a server `!` function serializes its error variant across the boundary.
